examples.title: Navigable link rows
examples.description: Passing `href` turns the `title` snippet into an `<a>`, making the whole row a navigable link.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { DataList } from '@lostgradient/cinder';
  import { StackedListItem } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  const docs = [
    { id: 'getting-started', name: 'Getting started', href: '#getting-started' },
    { id: 'theming', name: 'Theming', href: '#theming' },
    { id: 'accessibility', name: 'Accessibility', href: '#accessibility' },
  ];
</script>

<DataList items={docs} key={(doc) => doc.id}>
  {#snippet children(doc)}
    <StackedListItem href={doc.href}>
      {#snippet title()}{doc.name}{/snippet}
    </StackedListItem>
  {/snippet}
</DataList>

examples.description: groupLayout="band" draws a group row as one line: the status dot outside a tinted band holding a chevron, the bold title, muted text and the toggle label. The missed runs of one schedule use the warning tone.

examples.title: Basic row
examples.description: A minimal StackedListItem with the required `title` snippet and a `meta` snippet, mounted inside the DataList container it is designed to compose with.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { DataList } from '@lostgradient/cinder';
  import { StackedListItem } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  const members = [
    { id: 'alice', name: 'Alice Chen', role: 'Engineer' },
    { id: 'bob', name: 'Bob Osei', role: 'Designer' },
    { id: 'carol', name: 'Carol Mwangi', role: 'Product' },
  ];
</script>

<DataList items={members} key={(member) => member.id}>
  {#snippet children(member)}
    <StackedListItem>
      {#snippet title()}{member.name}{/snippet}
      {#snippet meta()}{member.role}{/snippet}
    </StackedListItem>
  {/snippet}
</DataList>

examples.title: Chat list: status on line two
examples.description: The chat list is a recorded exception because its pane is too narrow for a leading column: line one is the bold title with the time, and line two is the status in a fixed-width column, then a one-line preview, so previews line up.
examples.code: chat.id} statusColumn> {#snippet children(chat)} {#snippet status()}{/snippet} {#snippet title()}{chat.title}{/snippet} {#snippet time()}{chat.time}{/snippet} {#snippet meta()}{chat.preview}{/snippet} {/snippet}

examples.title: A row that fails to load
examples.description: One failing row keeps its status, title and time on line one, and its `error` puts the message on line two beside a warning glyph with its own secondary Try again button. The rest of the list stays live; there is no banner.
examples.code:

examples.title: Glyph tile with actions
examples.description: leadingTone draws the leading glyph as a tinted tile; lines takes the two-line layout for a row with no status or time, and actions are secondary buttons.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { DataList, StackedListItem } from '@lostgradient/cinder';
  import CalendarX2 from '@lucide/svelte/icons/calendar-x-2';
</script>

<DataList items={['schedule']} key={(id) => id}>
  {#snippet children()}
    <StackedListItem
      lines
      leadingTone="warning"
      actions={[{ label: 'View schedule', href: '#daily-summary' }]}
    >
      {#snippet leading()}<CalendarX2 size={16} aria-hidden="true" />{/snippet}
      {#snippet title()}Daily summary missed 4 runs since Oct 30{/snippet}
      {#snippet description()}Interborough was off when it was due on Oct 30, Oct 31, Nov 1 and Nov
        2.{/snippet}
    </StackedListItem>
  {/snippet}
</DataList>

examples.title: Long values
examples.description: A long title clamps at two lines and a long line two ends in an ellipsis on one line, each carrying its full text as a tooltip. An unbroken identifier wraps anywhere instead of widening the page. The status column and the time never move.
examples.code: id} statusColumn> {#snippet children(id)} {#if id === 'digest'} {#snippet status()}{/snippet} {#snippet title()}{name}{/snippet} {#snippet time()}Next Fri Nov 6, 11:00 AM{/snippet} {#snippet meta()}{detail}{/snippet} {:else} {#snippet status()}{/snippet} {#snippet title()}{identifier}{/snippet} {#snippet time()}10:12 AM{/snippet} {#snippet meta()}Run · {identifier}{/snippet} {/if} {/snippet}

examples.title: Selected row
examples.description: selected marks the row open in the detail beside the list. It takes an accent tint that stays under the pointer, and sets aria-current on the row link.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { DataList, StackedListItem, StatusDot } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  const workers = [
    {
      id: 'reports',
      name: 'Reports worker',
      status: 'Disconnected' as const,
      heard: '1 h ago',
      meta: 'reports queue',
    },
    {
      id: 'payments',
      name: 'Payments worker 1',
      status: 'Connected' as const,
      heard: 'just now',
      meta: 'payments · 3 running',
    },
  ];
</script>

<DataList items={workers} key={(worker) => worker.id} statusColumn>
  {#snippet children(worker)}
    <StackedListItem
      href={`#${worker.id}`}
      selected={worker.id === 'reports'}
      tooltip={worker.name}
    >
      {#snippet status()}<StatusDot word={worker.status} />{/snippet}
      {#snippet title()}{worker.name}{/snippet}
      {#snippet time()}{worker.heard}{/snippet}
      {#snippet meta()}{worker.meta}{/snippet}
    </StackedListItem>
  {/snippet}
</DataList>

examples.title: Status-first two-line row
examples.description: Line one is a status dot and word in a fixed 128px column, a bold title and the time at the right edge; line two is muted meta that starts under the title. The whole row is one link, and an empty-status row keeps the column so titles line up.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import {
    DataList,
    StackedListItem,
    StatusDot,
    type StatusDotWordLabel,
  } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  type Run = {
    id: string;
    title: string;
    status: StatusDotWordLabel;
    time: string;
    meta: string;
  };

  const runs: Run[] = [
    {
      id: 'refund-4471',
      title: 'Refund order 4471',
      status: 'Waiting on you',
      time: '10:42 AM',
      meta: 'Chat · Tool runner · waiting 4 min',
    },
    {
      id: 'say-hello',
      title: 'Say hello',
      status: 'Done',
      time: '4:12 PM',
      meta: 'Chat · Assistant · 8 s',
    },
    {
      id: 'release-notes',
      title: 'Release notes',
      status: 'Failed',
      time: '11:00 AM',
      meta: 'Schedule · Release notes digest · failed at step 2 of 4 · GitHub didn’t answer (HTTP 503)',
    },
  ];

  const workflows = [
    {
      id: 'triage-inbox',
      title: 'Triage inbox',
      time: 'Oct 24',
      meta: '3 steps · 1 run · last ran Oct 24',
    },
  ];
</script>

<DataList items={runs} key={(run) => run.id} statusColumn>
  {#snippet children(run)}
    <StackedListItem href={`#${run.id}`} tooltip={run.title}>
      {#snippet status()}<StatusDot word={run.status} />{/snippet}
      {#snippet title()}{run.title}{/snippet}
      {#snippet time()}{run.time}{/snippet}
      {#snippet meta()}{run.meta}{/snippet}
    </StackedListItem>
  {/snippet}
</DataList>

<DataList items={workflows} key={(workflow) => workflow.id} statusColumn>

    <StackedListItem href={`#${workflow.id}`} tooltip={workflow.title}>

examples.title: Trailing actions that collapse on a phone
examples.description: Text actions at the end of a row are secondary buttons on a tablet or desktop and one More actions menu below 640px. A disabled action stays focusable and keeps its reason.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { DataList, StackedListItem } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  const agents = [
    {
      name: 'Assistant',
      chats: '12 chats · Answers questions and does general work',
      canChat: true,
    },
    {
      name: 'Release helper',
      chats: '0 chats · Held back while its plugin is disabled',
      canChat: false,
    },
  ];
</script>

<DataList items={agents} key={(agent) => agent.name}>
  {#snippet children(agent)}
    <StackedListItem
      actions={[
        { label: 'Memory', href: '#memory' },
        {
          label: 'New chat',
          href: '#new-chat',
          disabled: !agent.canChat,
          disabledReason: 'Connect a provider to start a chat',
        },
      ]}
    >
      {#snippet title()}{agent.name}{/snippet}
      {#snippet meta()}{agent.chats}{/snippet}
    </StackedListItem>
  {/snippet}
</DataList>

examples.title: With description and leading icon
examples.description: A richer row pairing a `leading` visual (here a StatusDot) with a `title` and a secondary `description` snippet below it.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { DataList } from '@lostgradient/cinder';
  import { StackedListItem } from '@lostgradient/cinder';
  import { StatusDot } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  const services = [
    {
      id: 'api',
      name: 'API gateway',
      detail: 'All regions healthy',
      status: 'online' as const,
      statusLabel: 'Online',
    },
    {
      id: 'db',
      name: 'Primary database',
      detail: 'Replication lag 1.2s',
      status: 'warning' as const,
      statusLabel: 'Warning',
    },
    {
      id: 'cache',
      name: 'Cache cluster',
      detail: 'Node 3 unreachable',
      status: 'danger' as const,
      statusLabel: 'Danger',
    },
  ];
</script>

<DataList items={services} key={(service) => service.id}>
  {#snippet children(service)}
    <StackedListItem>
      {#snippet leading()}
        <StatusDot status={service.status} label={service.statusLabel} />
      {/snippet}
      {#snippet title()}{service.name}{/snippet}
      {#snippet description()}{service.detail}{/snippet}
    </StackedListItem>
  {/snippet}
</DataList>

examples.title: A 380px list pane
examples.description: The phone layout keys on the viewport, not the container, so a 380px list pane on a desktop keeps its fixed status column; a long approval title clamps to two lines beside the status, with line two and the time keeping their place.
